etymology.text: 小时 ‘childhood’ (literally ‘small time’; Wiktionary lists this sense of 小时) + 候 ‘time, season’, as in 时候.

funFacts: 小时候 contains 小时 ‘hour’: 三个小时 ‘three hours’ but 小时候 ‘when I was little’ — read to the end of the word.
pitfalls: 小时候 is a time word: it stands before the verb or at the very start (我小时候… / 小时候我…), never after the verb.
It already means ‘when I was a child’ — no …的时候 is added.
subtleties: With 常常 / 总是 / 每天 it gives the ‘used to’ of childhood: 小时候我每天都玩 ‘I used to play every day’.

tradPerSense.none: traditional 小時候 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

measure.none: a time word: it is not counted

contrasts.value: written and reflective: childhood as a period, a noun (美好的童年)

etymology.text: 童 ‘child’ (as in 儿童 ‘children’) + 年 ‘years’: ‘the child years’.

funFacts: 儿童节 ‘Children’s Day’ (1 June in the mainland) shares the 童 of 童年.
pitfalls: 童年 does not open a sentence as ‘when I was a child’ on its own: say 我小时候住在北京, or in writing 童年时….
subtleties: 童年 sounds reflective — memoirs, songs, essays; in conversation people say 小时候.

etymology.text: 玩 ‘to play’ + 具 ‘tool, implement’ (as in 工具 ‘tool’): ‘a play-tool’.

funFacts: ‘Play with toys’ is 玩玩具 — the same character twice: wán wánjù.
pitfalls: Playing WITH a toy needs no word for ‘with’: the toy is the object, 玩玩具.
subtleties: 玩具 is a child’s toy; a grown-up’s gadget or ‘toy’ is jokingly 玩意儿.

etymology.text: 游 ‘to roam, to swim; to play’ + 戏 ‘play, show’ (as in 戏剧 ‘drama’).

funFacts: 游戏 is also the everyday word for video games: 打游戏 / 玩游戏 ‘play video games’.
pitfalls: A sports match is not 游戏 but 比赛 (C21): 足球比赛 ‘a football match’.
subtleties: 做游戏 is playing organised games (at school, at a party); 玩游戏 is any game, very often a video game.

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 ‘jade’ + phonetic 元 — the ancient toys made of jade (Wiktionary).

funFacts: 好玩 ‘fun’ is literally ‘good to play’: 北京很好玩 ‘Beijing is great fun’.
pitfalls: 玩 is not used for sports or instruments: 踢足球 ‘play football’, 打篮球 ‘play basketball’, 弹钢琴 ‘play the piano’ (C21).
subtleties: 去北京玩 is ‘go to Beijing for a good time’ — 玩 covers sightseeing and fun for adults too.

etymology.text: 长 zhǎng ‘to grow’ + 大 ‘big’: ‘grow big’ — a verb with its result.

funFacts: 长 zhǎng ‘to grow’ and 长 cháng ‘long’ are one character: 长大 ‘grow up’, but 很长 ‘very long’.
pitfalls: 长大 already has its result and takes no object (*长大孩子); ‘to bring up a child’ is 养大 / 带大.
subtleties: 你长大了！ ‘How you’ve grown!’ is a common thing to say to a child.

readings.none: one reading: zhǎngdà (alone, 长 is also cháng ‘long’, S16)

tradPerSense.none: traditional 長大 for every sense

etymology.text: 记 ‘to record, to remember’ + 得 (de, a verbal suffix, from 得 ‘to obtain’): ‘keep in mind’.

funFacts: 记得 + verb is also ‘remember to’: 记得给我打电话 ‘remember to call me’.
pitfalls: Negated with 不: 我不记得了 ‘I don’t remember (any more)’ — not *我没记得.
subtleties: 记得 is having it in memory; 记住 is getting it in (‘memorize, note’); 想起来 is suddenly recalling it.

etymology.text: 忘 ‘to forget’ + 记 ‘to remember, to record’: ‘lose from memory’.

funFacts: 忘 is 亡 ‘to lose, to vanish’ above 心 ‘heart’: what has vanished from the heart (Wiktionary).
pitfalls: Leaving something behind somewhere is 忘在: 我把护照忘在酒店了 ‘I left my passport at the hotel’ — the place follows 在.
subtleties: 忘记 sounds a little more careful than 忘了; the everyday cry is 我忘了！

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

contrasts.value: short and spoken, mostly as 忘了 (我忘了！)

synonyms.nuance: wàngjì: forget — the full word
wàngdiào: forget completely

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亡 + semantic 心 ‘heart’. Originally the same word as 亡 ‘to lose, to disappear’, later with a perfective suffix: ‘it has disappeared (from the mind)’ (Schuessler 2007, via Wiktionary). A doublet of 忙.

funFacts: 忘 (wàng) and 忙 (máng ‘busy’) are both 亡 + heart — 忙 puts the heart at the side; Wiktionary calls them doublets.
pitfalls: 忘 alone is rare: say 忘了 or 忘记 — 我忘了他的名字, not *我忘他的名字.
subtleties: 别忘了 ‘don’t forget’ is one of the most frequent reminders of daily speech.

etymology.text: A calque of German Kindergarten (Wiktionary): 幼儿 ‘small children’ + 园 ‘garden’.

funFacts: 幼儿园 is a word-for-word translation of German Kindergarten — ‘small-children garden’.
pitfalls: 幼稚 alone means ‘childish, naive’: calling an adult 幼稚 is an insult, even though 幼稚园 is the Taiwan word for kindergarten.
subtleties: Children go to 幼儿园 from about three to six, then to 小学 ‘primary school’.

subtleties: 邻居 is one neighbour or all of them: 我的邻居 — the number comes from context or 们 (邻居们).

etymology.text: 暑 ‘summer heat’ + 假 jià ‘leave, time off’: ‘the heat holiday’.

subtleties: In China the summer holidays usually run from July to the end of August; school starts again in September.

etymology.text: 寒 ‘cold’ + 假 jià ‘leave, time off’: ‘the cold holiday’.

funFacts: The winter holidays are built around the Spring Festival, so their dates move every year with the lunar calendar.
pitfalls: 寒假 is for schools and universities; working people get the much shorter 春节假期.
subtleties: 寒 is the literary ‘cold’; in speech ‘cold’ is 冷 (S16), but the holiday keeps 寒.

absent.reason: No word and no verb form for the habitual past: Chinese uses a past time word with the plain verb.
absent.use: 以前 / 小时候 / 那时候 + (常常, 总是, 每天 …) + verb, without 了: 我小时候常常去奶奶家 ‘I used to go to Grandma’s’; 以前我不喝咖啡 ‘I didn’t use to drink coffee’. The change since then: 现在 … 了 (现在我喝了).
